findings.comment: Point of service location is not explicitly marked or labeled on any of the required plan sheets. The plans show electrical infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground lines) but do not identify the specific point where Austin Energy's infrastructure connects to the customer's electrical system. The POS must be clearly designated on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows an underground electric line entry point from Valley View Road on the western boundary, but does not include an explicit label or designation identifying this as the 'Point of Service' (POS) per UCM § 1.3.4. The plan shows transformer pads and meters but no specific POS location marker. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a single transformer pad labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' without identifying which location serves as the point of service connection to Austin Energy infrastructure. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only overhead electric lines along the boundary, with no POS designation. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, the POS must be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires that the point of electric service be shown on plan sheets. UCM § 1.3.4 defines POS as 'the location where Austin Energy's and the Customer's conductors are connected or terminated.' The presence of transformer pads and underground line routing does not constitute a clear POS designation. Without an explicit label identifying which location serves as the official POS, the requirement is not met. The applicant must clearly designate the POS location on all required sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

findings.comment: Point of service (POS) location is not explicitly labeled on any required plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows electrical routing and infrastructure but lacks a clear 'Point of Service' designation. Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 do not adequately identify the POS. Add explicit POS labeling to Site Plan (Sheet 9), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) showing where Austin Energy infrastructure connects to proposed customer infrastructure.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts electrical infrastructure including transformers, pull boxes, and meters, but does NOT contain an explicit label designating the Point of Service (POS). The plan shows where proposed underground electric lines enter from Valley View Road (western property line) and connect to electrical pull boxes, but the specific connection point to Austin Energy infrastructure is not labeled as 'Point of Service' or 'POS'. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only a single 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' without identifying the POS or primary source. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows overhead electric lines on boundaries but no identification of POS. The grouping's regulatory overview (UCM § 1.16.0) requires the POS to be clearly designated, and unless otherwise specified by Austin Energy, the POS must be shown on the required plan sheets (site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) and § 1.4.2.6 require that the point of service designation be shown on all required plan sheets (site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans). While Sheet 21 depicts the general electrical routing and infrastructure, the POS is not explicitly labeled or designated. Without clear labeling of the POS location, a reviewer cannot confirm compliance with the requirement to show the 'desired point of electric service' on the plans. This is distinct from merely showing infrastructure; the POS must be explicitly identified as the location where Austin Energy's and the Customer's conductors connect or terminate per UCM § 1.3.4.

findings.comment: Point of electric service (POS) location is not explicitly designated on required plan sheets. Add clear labeling of the point of service location (meter socket, pedestal, pull-box, or AE-designated enclosure) on all required sheets per UCM § 1.16.0(6) and UCM § 1.4.2.6.
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing originating from west side of property but no specific label for "Point of Service" or "POS"; the connection point is shown but not explicitly designated as the POS per AE Design requirements. Sheet 9 shows a single transformer pad but no POS designation. Sheet 31 shows only overhead electric line on boundary, no POS marked. The point of service location and primary source location are not clearly labeled or designated on any of the required plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires the point of electric service to be shown on plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 requirements. While Sheet 21 shows electrical infrastructure and apparent connection points, these are not explicitly labeled as the "Point of Service" or identified as the location where Austin Energy's and the customer's conductors connect. Per UCM § 1.3.4, the POS is the specific location of connection or termination. The absence of explicit POS designation on required sheets (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) means the POS location cannot be verified as shown per code requirements. On Sheet 21, while the general routing is shown, the specific POS is not called out.

findings.comment: Electric meter locations are shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) but are missing from the Site Plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and the Landscape Plan (Sheet 31). Electric meter locations must be clearly marked on all required plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows multiple locations labeled 'Electrical Meters' on the exterior walls of various buildings (visible on north walls of Buildings 1, 3, and 4; south walls of Buildings 2, 7, and 8) indicating meter banks or grouped meters. However, Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) does not show or label any electric meter locations on any of the building footprints. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows no meter locations marked. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, electric meter locations must be shown on the site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 defines the Point of Service (POS) and per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, all electrical plans and the site plan showing all utilities must depict meter locations. While Sheet 21 shows meter callouts indicating meter locations on buildings, the required sheets per the standard (Site Plan showing all utilities and Landscape Plan) do not indicate where meters are located. Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 fail to show meter locations, creating incomplete documentation of this required infrastructure element.

findings.comment: Electric meter locations are not shown on Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), despite these being required plan sheets. Add meter locations to both sheets showing where all electrical meters are positioned on the building exteriors, consistent with the locations shown on the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electric meter locations clearly labeled as 'Electrical Meters' on building exteriors (north walls of Bldgs. 1, 3, 4, 5; south walls of Bldgs. 6, 7; west walls of Bldgs. 2, 8). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not display meter locations - the vision analysis found no meter symbols or labels on this sheet despite it being identified as showing 'all utilities.' Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also does not show meter locations. The meters are confined to Sheet 21 only, and absent from the two required plan sheets (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) that must show utility infrastructure per UCM § 1.4.2.6.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 (Point of Service definition) and UCM § 1.4.2.6 (Customer Drawings Specifications) require electric meter locations to be shown on all required plan sheets including the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan. While the Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) contains this information, the requirement specifies that the information must appear on the site plan and landscape plan. Absence of meter locations from Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) means these required sheets do not adequately document the electrical service infrastructure for review. This prevents verification of meter grouping, spacing, and coordination with other site elements per the meter requirements in UCM § 1.5.2.1(G).

findings.comment: Electric meter locations must be shown on site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) in addition to the electrical plan. Add labels identifying the location and number of electrical meters serving each building per UCM § 1.3.4.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 8 electrical meter locations, labeled "Electrical Meters" at specific building locations (north wall of Bldg 1, north wall of Bldg 3, east wall of Bldg 5, south wall of Bldg 2, south wall of Bldg 4, east wall of Bldg 6, south wall of Bldg 7, south wall of Bldg 8). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does NOT show any electrical meter locations - despite showing other utilities (water, sewer, storm) and one transformer pad. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show any electrical meter locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 defines the Point of Service and requires its location to be shown. The electrical meter locations are critical to identifying the customer's service equipment and POS. UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires all electrical plans and the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan to include electric infrastructure. The absence of meter locations on Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) means these required sheets do not show the complete electric service infrastructure. The customer's service equipment (meters) must be shown on all required plan sheets for proper utility coordination and to verify POS compliance.

findings.comment: Transformer locations must be shown on all required plan sheets. Currently shown only on electrical plan (Sheet 21) and site plan (Sheet 9). Missing from wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer locations with associated routing and infrastructure. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)'. However, transformers are NOT depicted on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), Sheet 11 (Grading Plan), Sheet 19 (Wet Utilities Plan), or Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile). Although Sheet 19 and 20 include a 'Transformer Pad' symbol in their legends, no transformers are actually drawn on these sheets.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, transformer locations must be georeferenced on all required plan sheets to facilitate utility coordination and ensure proper design integration across all disciplines. The grouping guidance specifies that 'Transformer locations must be shown consistently across multiple plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and elevation sheets)' and that 'grading and storm plans must also show transformers when those disciplines are affected by transformer placement or routing.' Omitting transformers from the wet utilities, landscape, and grading plans means these critical disciplines have not integrated the electrical infrastructure and cannot verify conflicts, clearances, or impacts.

findings.comment: Transformer locations are not shown consistently across all required plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads, Sheet 9 shows 1 transformer, and Sheets 11, 12, 19, and 31 show no transformers. Add transformer locations to site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan. Ensure all transformer locations are consistent across all sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 4 transformer pads with locations in northwest, southwest, northeast, and southeast areas of the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1 transformer pad labeled "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" near Building 1. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains legend symbols for transformer pads but no actual transformer pads are drawn on the plan. Sheets 11 (Grading Plan), 12 (Storm Sewer Plan), and 31 (Landscape Plan) do not show any transformer locations. This creates significant inconsistency: 4 transformers are documented on the electrical plan but only 1 appears on the main site plan, and transformers are entirely absent from the wet utilities, grading, storm, and landscape plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that georeferenced AutoCAD drawings clearly delineate electrical infrastructure locations across all required plan sheets. The standard sheet set for transformer documentation includes site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading/storm plans when applicable. The variance between sheets—with Sheet 21 showing 4 transformers and Sheet 9 showing only 1—indicates either incomplete documentation on the site plan or an incomplete electrical design on Sheet 21. The complete absence of transformers from Sheets 19, 31, 11, and 12 prevents verification of clearances, conflicts with other utilities, and tree preservation impacts. For a multi-building development with 4 transformers, omitting transformers from landscape and grading plans prevents the reviewer from verifying required clearances and access routes.

findings.comment: Transformer locations shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) must match the transformer locations shown on Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) in terms of quantity, position, and labeling. Currently, Sheet 9 shows one transformer marked '(Typ.)' while Sheet 21 shows four transformers with specific locations.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four distinct transformer pad locations distributed across the site (west of Building 1, west of Buildings 2/8, east of Building 4, and south-central between Buildings 6/7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only one transformer location labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)', positioned in the western area of the site. The single transformer shown on Sheet 9 appears to align roughly with the western area where transformers are shown on Sheet 21, but the representation is unclear. The notation '(Typ.)' on Sheet 9 suggests this is a typical or representative symbol rather than a precise location.
findings.reasoning: Transformer locations must be consistent across all plan sheets showing them so that all disciplines and reviewing agencies have a unified understanding of the infrastructure layout. When the same facilities appear on different sheets (site plan, electrical plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, grading plan), their locations should match precisely. The ambiguous representation on Sheet 9 (with a single '(Typ.)' notation) does not align clearly with the four transformers shown on Sheet 21, creating confusion about the actual number and locations of transformers on the site.

findings.comment: Transformer locations are not consistent across plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads while Sheet 9 shows only 1 transformer. Reconcile transformer locations and ensure all transformers appear on all required plan sheets with consistent positioning.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 depicts 4 transformer pads: one in the northwest area (west of Buildings 1 and 2), one in the southwest area (west of Building 8), one in the northeast central area (east of Building 4), and one in the southeast central area (east of Building 7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts only 1 transformer pad labeled "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" located near Building 1 (northwest area). The three transformers shown on Sheet 21 (southwest, northeast, southeast) are entirely absent from Sheet 9.
findings.reasoning: Transformer locations on Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) show 4 transformer pads, but Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1. This discrepancy violates the requirement for consistent documentation across plan sheets. Reconcile the transformer count and locations between sheets. Ensure all proposed transformers are shown on both the main site plan and the electrical design plan, with matching locations.

findings.comment: Meter locations must be shown and labeled on the site plan (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) in addition to the electrical plan (Sheet 21).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows eight meter locations on building exterior walls, with each labeled 'Electrical Meters.' However, meters are NOT shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) - vision analysis confirmed 'There are no electrical meters shown or labeled on this sheet.' Meters are also NOT shown on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) - vision analysis confirmed 'There are no... meters shown or labeled on this sheet.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.A, meter locations must be shown on all required plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan). This allows all reviewing disciplines to verify meter accessibility, line of sight to transformers, separation from other utilities, and landscape or site features that might interfere with meter access or visibility. Omitting meters from the site and landscape plans means these disciplines have not verified meter integration with their designs.

findings.comment: Meter locations not shown on all required plan sheets. Show all electrical meter locations on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. Identify each meter location with a callout and label. Note whether meters are grouped (per UCM § 1.9.3.4) or individual. Verify that each meter location is: (1) at ground level, (2) readily accessible, (3) within sight of its serving transformer, and (4) positioned with disconnects within 20 feet for grouped configurations.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 8 meter locations labeled "Electrical Meters" on building exterior walls. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one gas meter but does not show electrical meter locations. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has a legend entry for utility symbols but no meters are drawn on the plan. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show electrical meter locations. The required site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan all lack electrical meter documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.A requires meter locations to be shown on plans. Meters must be on first floor or ground level, readily accessible, within sight of the transformer, and for grouped metering, positioned with disconnects in a common location per UCM § 1.9.3.4. The absence of meter locations on the site plan and landscape plan prevents verification of accessibility, sightlines to transformers, and clearances from other utilities. For a multi-unit development, meter locations are essential to demonstrating that the metering and disconnection configuration complies with grouped metering requirements.

findings.comment: Street lighting layout and light pole locations are not shown on the Site Plan (Sheet 9) or Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), though the site has public street frontage on Valley View Road. If street lighting is required per Austin Energy Design determination, the layout and pole locations must be shown on the site plan and landscape plan per UCM § 1.4.2.6. Confirm with AE Design whether street lighting is required for this project and provide documentation of the determination.
findings.observation: The site plan shows the development abuts Valley View Road to the west. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows street frontage along Valley View Road and references street improvement requirements in the general notes ('For construction within the right-of-way, a ROW excavation permit is required'). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows a street yard area along Valley View Road (labeled with H.2 'STREET YARD' symbol). Neither Sheet 9 nor Sheet 31 shows any street lighting layout, light pole locations, or street lighting infrastructure marked or labeled. The project appears to include public street frontage triggering street lighting applicability per UCM § 1.6.0, which directs customers to 'contact AE Design' for specific requirements. No indication of street lighting coordination or requirements is present in the visible plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.6.0 addresses Street Lighting requirements. The grouping's applicability guidance states street lighting applies when 'site includes or abuts public streets requiring street lighting.' This site has frontage on Valley View Road (a local street per facts.md), which would typically require street lighting evaluation. The grouping notes that 'specific street lighting requirements are determined by contacting AE Design' and the applicant should verify coordination with AE Design. The absence of any street lighting layout or infrastructure markings on Sheets 9 and 31 (the Site Plan and Landscape Plan where street lighting must be shown per UCM § 1.4.2.6) constitutes non-compliance unless AE Design has waived street lighting for this project. Documentation of AE Design waiver or determination is not visible in available documents.

findings.comment: Cannot verify whether street lighting is required for this site from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required for the Valley View Road frontage per UCM § 1.6.0. If required, show street light layout and pole locations on site plan and landscape plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) were examined for street lighting layout and light pole locations. Sheet 9 includes a Lighting Note addressing "exterior lighting" (building wall-mounted lights), not street lighting infrastructure. No street lighting, light poles, or photometric layouts are shown on either sheet. Facts.md indicates Valley View Road is classified as a local street (ASMP Level 1) with existing lane count not on file and a 2-undivided-lane cross-section planned. The site plan does not show street improvements along Valley View Road frontage that would typically trigger street lighting requirements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.6.0 requires street lighting to be shown when required, and the grouping notes state to "Check: Site plan for street frontage and street improvement requirements; contact AE Design business unit for street lighting determination." The absence of explicit street improvement requirements on Valley View Road frontage and the absence of street lighting from the plans suggest it may not be required. However, the determination cannot be made from site plan review alone per UCM § 1.6.0 - it requires direct contact with AE Design. The checklist item states this determination "cannot be determined from plans alone" and must be verified through AE Design coordination, which does not appear to have been completed or documented.

findings.comment: Street light conduit plan, conduit connections, and routing are not shown on any of the required plan sheets (Site Plan, Landscape Plan, Electrical Plans). If street lighting is required for this project, complete conduit plans must be provided per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. Confirm street lighting requirements with Austin Energy Design.
findings.observation: No street lighting conduit plan, conduit routing, or conduit connections are shown on any of the reviewed sheets (Sheet 9, 21, or 31). The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows only building service conduit routing and meter connections, with no separate street lighting conduit layer or specifications. Sheets 9 and 31 show no lighting conduit markings. Per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B, if street lighting is required, the conduit plan must be shown on the site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.6.0 governs Street Lighting. If street lighting is applicable to this project (site has Valley View Road frontage per facts.md), then the street light conduit plan, connections, and routing must be shown per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B on the site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans. The complete absence of street lighting conduit documentation on all sheets constitutes a deficiency if street lighting is required. This must be confirmed with AE Design and, if required, the conduit plans must be added.

findings.comment: Cannot determine applicability from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required. If required, provide street light conduit plan showing conduit connections and routing on site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.6.0.
findings.observation: No street light conduit, conduit connections, or conduit routing are shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), or Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan). As noted in EL-17.7 findings, street lighting infrastructure is not visible anywhere in the plan set. The applicability of this item depends on whether street lighting is required, which per UCM § 1.6.0 must be determined by contacting Austin Energy Design.
findings.reasoning: Per the checklist item's applicability note, this item applies "Only when street lighting or parking garage lighting is required." The grouping's regulatory overview (Section 8 of grouping file) states: "Specific street lighting requirements are determined by contacting AE Design (UCM § 1.6.0)." Without documentation of AE Design's determination regarding street lighting applicability, this item's applicability cannot be confirmed. If street lighting is determined to be required by AE Design, then the absence of street light conduit plans would be a deficiency.

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations must be shown on all plan sheets (site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, grading plan, and storm plan when applicable). Currently, transformers are detailed only on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan), with one typical example on Sheet 9 (Site Plan). Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11), and Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12) do not show any transformer locations. Revise all affected sheets to depict the five transformer pad locations with consistent positioning and labeling.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) depicts 5 transformer pads with specific locations and underground electric routing to all 8 buildings. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1 transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' - a single representative symbol without depicting all 5 transformers. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show any transformer pad locations. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) does not show any transformer pad locations. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show any transformer pad locations. The Wet Utilities Plan (Sheet 19) has a legend including transformer symbols but contains no actual electrical infrastructure. Therefore, transformer locations are NOT shown consistently or completely on all required plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires transformer locations shown on site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading/storm plans when applicable. This site has 39 units served by 5 transformers, which should be visible on all plan sheets. Sheet 21 provides detailed electrical information with 5 transformers, but the required discipline plans (landscape, grading, storm) are completely missing this critical infrastructure. Sheet 9 shows only a typical example, not the actual site layout with all 5 transformers. The absence of transformers on landscape and grading plans means Austin Energy and the City cannot verify clearances, access, or conflicts on those plans.

findings.comment: Transformer locations shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) are not consistent with Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). Sheet 9 shows one typical example while Sheet 21 shows 5 specific transformer locations. Revise Sheet 9 to show all 5 transformer locations in their actual positions on the site.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 5 transformer pads with specific locations: northwest (west of Bldg. 1), west-central (west of Bldg. 2), southwest (south of Bldg. 8), east-central (between Bldg. 4 and 5), and southeast (south of Bldg. 6). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1 transformer labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' on the west side south of the main driveway, located between the driveway and Building 8 near a tree well. The single transformer on Sheet 9 is labeled as typical (representative), not showing the actual locations of all 5 transformers required to serve the 8 buildings and 39 units.
findings.reasoning: Transformer locations must be consistent across all plan sheets to enable verification of clearances, conflicts, and infrastructure coordination. Sheet 9 and Sheet 21 show different numbers of transformers and different levels of detail. Sheet 9 appears to show only an example of what a transformer pad symbol looks like, not the actual site-specific locations. This inconsistency creates confusion about which transformers are actually proposed and prevents comprehensive review of clearances and conflicts on the site plan.

findings.comment: Add a legend to Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identifying all proposed electrical utilities with symbols and descriptions, including: Transformer Pad, Electrical Meter, Pull Box, Underground Electric Line, and any other electrical facilities shown. Also add or enhance the legend on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to clearly show proposed electrical infrastructure symbols. Ensure symbols are consistent with any legend shown on other utility plan sheets (Sheets 19, 20).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) does not include a title block legend or notation delineating transformers, meters, and pull boxes as proposed utilities. The plan has leader lines pointing to individual equipment with text labels ('Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Meters', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Underground Electric Line') but no formal legend or symbol key is shown on the sheet. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) mentions overhead electric lines but shows limited electrical symbols. No formal legend on either sheet identifies proposed electrical utilities with symbols and explains what each symbol represents.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that proposed utilities be clearly delineated in plan legends. A proper legend helps readers understand the plan symbols and ensures consistency across all sheets. Without a legend on the electrical plans identifying transformers, meters, pull boxes, and underground lines as proposed utilities, the plans are incomplete. Other disciplines reviewing the electrical plans must have clear symbol definitions.

findings.comment: Meter locations must be shown on all required plan sheets. Add 8 meter locations to: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan) - mark meter positions on each building; (2) Sheet 19 or 20 (Wet Utilities Plan) - show meter positions relative to water, wastewater, and storm drain utilities; (3) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) - show meter positions to verify clearances from plantings. Label all meters with unique identifiers matching the electrical plan.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations labeled as 'Electrical Meters' positioned on or near each of the 8 buildings (Bldg. 1-8). However: (1) Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show meter locations - no meters are labeled or visible; (2) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show meter locations - vision analysis confirmed 'No meter locations are shown or labeled'; (3) Sheet 19 (Wet Utilities Plan) contains a legend that includes symbols for meters but no actual meter locations are depicted on the plan drawing. Therefore, meter locations are NOT shown on all required plan sheets as specified in the checklist.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.A requires meter locations shown on site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. This allows review of meter accessibility, visibility to transformer, and clearance from other utilities and building features. Sheet 21 shows meters but they must also be shown on the Site Plan, Wet Utilities Plan, and Landscape Plan for complete coordination.

findings.comment: Existing transformer pad shown on survey (Sheet 4) must be depicted and labeled as 'Existing' or 'EX' on all applicable plan sheets, with notation indicating whether it will be retained, removed, or replaced.
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) depicts an existing transformer pad in the southeast corner of the property with a clear label 'TRANSFORMER PAD' visible in the bottom right area, along with existing overhead electric lines (OHE) and utility poles (marked TYP.). However, this existing transformer pad is NOT shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), or Sheet 11 (Grading Plan). The demolition plan (Sheet 8) notes 'Coordinate with City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines' but makes no specific reference to the existing transformer pad, and it is not marked for removal or abandonment.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, when existing electrical facilities are present on a site, their locations must be shown on all applicable plan sheets. This informs Austin Energy and other stakeholders whether the existing transformer is being retained, abandoned, replaced, or relocated. The absence of the existing transformer from the new development plans creates ambiguity about its disposition and prevents clear visual coordination of existing vs. proposed infrastructure. The grouping guidance states: 'Transformer locations must be shown consistently across multiple plan sheets' and specifies this applies 'when existing transformers present on site.'

findings.comment: If transformer screening is proposed, show on site plan, landscape plan, and grading plan: screening wall/fence extent and dimensions, door swing clearances relative to screening, and landscape plantings around screening. If no screening is proposed, note 'No Screening' on electrical plan.
findings.observation: Vision analysis of all plan sheets confirms no transformer screening is shown. Sheet 21 electrical plan shows transformer pads as basic symbols with no screening details. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) makes no reference to transformer screening or landscape treatment around electrical equipment. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not indicate screening. No notes, elevations, or details show whether screening walls, fencing, berms, or landscaping are planned around the transformers.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, when transformer screening is proposed to mitigate visual impact, site plans must clearly show 'Transformer screening extent, dimensions, and door swings on all plan sheets (site, grading, landscape).' This ensures that screening design does not interfere with required clearance zones or door operations, and allows Austin Energy to verify access compatibility. Screening details are also necessary for architectural and landscape integration review.

findings.comment: Transformer labels missing on required sheets or inconsistent. Establish consistent labeling (e.g., "Electrical Transformer Pad - Type [X], Size [Y] kVA") and show transformers on all required sheets: site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan (where applicable). Use a standard notation on all sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels transformers as "Electrical Transformer Pad" on the electrical plan. Sheet 9 labels one transformer as "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" on the site plan. Sheets 19, 31, 11, and 12 contain no transformer labels whatsoever because transformers are not depicted on these sheets. The irregular labeling, combined with the absence of transformers from required sheets, means that the reviewer cannot verify consistent identification of electrical infrastructure across the document set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that electrical infrastructure be clearly labeled on all required plan sheets. Consistent, informative labeling enables Austin Energy and the City to verify that all proposed equipment is accounted for and properly identified across all disciplines. The current labeling is inconsistent ("Electrical Transformer Pad" vs. "Transformer Pad (Typ.)") and incomplete (missing from landscape, wet utilities, grading, and storm plans). This prevents confident cross-reference of electrical equipment across the plan set.

findings.comment: Transformers not delineated in legend as proposed utilities. Add a Utility Legend to the site plan, wet utilities plan, and electrical plan defining the symbols for: (1) Transformer Pad, (2) Proposed Underground Electric Line, (3) Electrical Meter, (4) Electrical Easement, and (5) Pull Box. Use consistent symbols across all sheets. Ensure symbols are actually applied on the plans.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) contains no utility legend. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) contains no utility legend defining transformer or meter symbols. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains a Legend in the top-right corner that defines two electrical symbols: "- E - Proposed Underground Electric" and "[Square symbol] Transformer Pad". However, on Sheet 19, neither of these symbols are actually drawn on the plan—the legend defines symbols that are not used. Sheets 11, 12, and 31 contain no transformer symbols or legends.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires plans to delineate proposed utilities clearly. A utility legend is the standard method for communicating utility symbols and line types. The absence of a consistent legend across the site plan set, combined with the fact that the legend on Sheet 19 defines symbols that are not actually used, violates the clarity requirement. Austin Energy and City reviewers expect a unified legend identifying all proposed electrical infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground lines, easements) with symbols consistently applied across all relevant sheets.

findings.comment: Show and label the existing meter (with 'EX' or 'Existing' notation) on the electrical plan, site plan, and landscape plan. Include notation indicating whether it will be abandoned, removed, or retained and integrated into the new service design.
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) clearly shows an existing electrical meter labeled 'ELEC. METER' attached to the exterior wall of the main building structure. However, this existing meter is NOT shown on Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), NOT shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and NOT shown on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). The demolition plan (Sheet 8) does not specifically reference the existing electrical meter, nor is it marked for removal or abandonment.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.16.0, when existing electrical facilities are present on a site, their locations must be shown on all applicable plan sheets. Similar to the existing transformer, the existing meter disposition must be clear: is it being retained, removed, or replaced? Without showing the existing meter on the development plans, there is ambiguity about its status and how it relates to the new electrical service design.
